candidates.title: Electromagnetic System Conceptual Design for a Negative Triangularity Tokamak
candidates.notes: Pre-conceptual electromagnetic system design for dedicated NT tokamak experiment (R0=1m, Bt=3T, 16 demountable Cu TF coils). Addresses passive stabilizing plate integration: HFS+LFS plates together reduce vertical instability growth rates by ~75%. Quantifies net forces on stabilizer plates (~28 kN/m inboard, ~16 kN/m outboard) and notes 'significantly increased structural support will likely be required.' Directly fills G-15 — provides the engineering-level treatment of passive stabilizer plate design and mechanical loading absent from MANTA.

candidates.title: Assessment of vertical stability for negative triangularity pilot plants
candidates.notes: Already in sources as arxiv-2401-15217 (extracted in iter-2 for G-14). Provides baseline vertical stability analysis; 2501.14682 is the follow-on engineering design.

candidates.title: The ARIES Advanced and Conservative Tokamak (ACT)
candidates.notes: Full ARIES-ACT technical paper (distinct from UCSD-CER-13-01 cost account doc already extracted). 2.8MB PDF — WebFetch could not read binary content, but add-source has proper extraction. Likely contains CAS-level cost breakdowns for ACT1/ACT2 including divertor as distinct line items. Useful as PT baseline for G-8 cost differential estimate.

candidates.title: Optimizing the cost of the STEP programme
candidates.notes: Not triaged due to WebFetch budget exhaustion. STEP is a UK government ST/tokamak program — may contain cost breakdown data but likely not NT-vs-PT specific.

gaps_attempted.notes: No source found that specifically quantifies NT vs. PT divertor cost differential. ARIES-ACT 1127358 provides PT tokamak divertor cost as a line item (PT baseline). NT advantage can only be derived by comparing MANTA's divertor conditions (2.8 MW/m^2 peak, 23.5 MW P_SOL) vs. ACT1/ACT2 divertor conditions and inferring cost savings from simpler design requirements.
